record.paper_title: Everything You Always Wanted to Know About How Causal Set Theory Can Help with Open Questions in Cosmology, but Were Afraid to Ask
record.original_question: Can covariant ultraviolet-cutoff predictions for primordial power spectra in quantum field theory on curved spacetime be realized or sharpened inside causal set theory, where Green functions, d'Alembertian operators, and an intrinsic covariant ultraviolet cutoff are available?

evidence.quote: There is also a recent direction of work that has made predictions for a signature of a covariant UV cutoff at the level of quantum field theory in curved spacetime.

Many of the ingredients of this work (e.g. Green functions and d’Alembertians) are available in causal set theory as well, in addition to it being a concrete example of a theory with an intrinsic and covariant UV cutoff.
It would be interesting to explore whether these predictions can be realized or sharpened in the context of causal sets.

artifact.category_tag: causal set theory and covariant UV cutoffs
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a globally hyperbolic Lorentzian spacetime $(M,g)$ and a free scalar quantum field theory on it, with retarded/advanced Green functions $G^{\pm}$ of the d'Alembertian $\Box_g = g^{\mu\nu}\nabla_\mu \nabla_\nu$. A causal set is a locally finite partially ordered set $(C,\preceq)$, intended to model spacetime at the Planck scale; for a fixed sprinkling density $\rho$, a causal set is obtained from $(M,g)$ by a Poisson process on $M$ with intensity $\rho\,dV_g$, with the induced causal order. On causal sets, discrete analogues of the retarded Green function $G^{+}_C$ and of the scalar d'Alembertian $B_C$ are defined (e.g., via the Benincasa–Dowker family of operators) such that, in the continuum limit, expectations recover $G^{+}$ and $\Box_g$ respectively. The discreteness scale $\rho^{-1/d}$ provides an intrinsic, Lorentz-covariant ultraviolet cutoff.

In quantum field theory on a Friedmann–Lemaître–Robertson–Walker (FLRW) cosmological background, certain models implement a covariant ultraviolet cutoff at the QFT level and predict modifications of the primordial power spectrum of curvature perturbations of the form
$$\mathcal{P}(k) = \mathcal{P}_0(k)\bigl(1 + F(k/k_{\mathrm{UV}})\bigr),$$
where $k_{\mathrm{UV}}$ is the covariant cutoff scale and $F$ is a model-specific correction encoding the cutoff signature.

Formulate, within causal set theory on an FLRW background, a derivation of the two-point function of a scalar field perturbation using the causal-set Green functions $G^{+}_C$ and d'Alembertian $B_C$ together with the intrinsic discreteness cutoff at scale $\rho^{-1/d}$, and determine the corresponding prediction for the primordial scalar power spectrum $\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{CS}}(k;\rho)$. Specifically: (i) show whether $\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{CS}}(k;\rho)$ reproduces, in an appropriate continuum limit, the covariant-UV-cutoff predictions of the form above, and (ii) determine whether the causal-set framework sharpens these predictions, e.g. by fixing the form of $F$ uniquely from the discreteness scale $\rho^{-1/d}$, by computing subleading corrections, or by yielding observable signatures distinct from those of QFT-level covariant cutoffs.
artifact.status_search_result: This is posed as a research direction at the interface of causal set theory and cosmological perturbation theory. No published derivation realizing or sharpening the QFT covariant-UV-cutoff primordial power spectrum predictions inside causal set theory appears to have been completed; related work on causal-set scalar field two-point functions exists but does not provide a definitive answer to this question.

status_evidence.title: Causal set theory and cosmology (review)
status_evidence.snippet: Identifies the realization/sharpening of covariant UV-cutoff power spectrum predictions inside causal set theory as an open direction worth exploring.
status_evidence.claim: The question is stated as an open research direction.
